subject: Hosted API eval — quickstart, endpoints & rate limits

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>

Subject: Hosted API eval — quickstart, endpoints & rate limits

Hi Samantha / Tom,

Thanks again for your time today — appreciated the product context and the goals you shared (reduce latency for user-facing summaries, stay under $X per 1M tokens, and keep customer data segmented). A quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Recap: We walked through the hosted API demo (streaming generation, tool calls, embeddings for similarity), and showed how prefix caching and batching can reduce cost.
- Open questions from our side: peak RPS distribution, expected prompt+response token lengths, and any compliance constraints (PCI/PHI).
- Your asks: a quickstart guide to hit a PoC with Hosted API, concrete rate limit guidance, and whether Dedicated or Private modes are necessary given your SLAs.

Next steps:
1) I attached a one-page quickstart (redwood-quickstart.pdf) and a rate-limits note (rate-limits.md).
2) Aditya (cc) will scope a short SRE checklist to verify compatibility with AcmeApp's traffic pattern.
3) If the Hosted API looks good for PoC, we'll provide a 2-week test key and a sample eval harness.

If you can send estimated RPS and average token sizes, we can recommend whether Hosted will meet latency/SLOs or if Dedicated would be a better fit.

Thanks,

—Marissa

Answers:
- Peak traffic: ~180 requests/minute during peak (bursty), average 40 req/min sustained. Most requests are short prompts (~50 tokens) with ~150 tokens generated on average.
- Compliance: we do not handle PCI/PHI but must ensure customer PII is not retained.
- SLA: target p95 latency < 300ms for generation.

Question: With the burstiness, is Hosted API likely to throttle us? If so, we may need Dedicated for consistent p95. Also curious about the rate limits per API key and per-account.

Thanks — happy to chat for 15 mins if helpful.

—Samantha

samantha@acmeapp.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-22T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API eval — quickstart, endpoints & rate limits

Thanks for the details, Samantha — super helpful. Quick answers and a recommended path for PoC.

Inline:
- Burstiness: Hosted API enforces per-key and per-account rate limits to protect SLOs. Typical default is 300 requests/min per key with token-rate enforcement; burst handling uses a small token bucket and we support short bursts above sustained quotas. For your numbers (peaks ~180 req/min and avg ~40), Hosted should be fine out of the box. If you see sustained higher peaks, Dedicated is recommended.
- Latency: For short prompts + ~150 tokens response, we've observed p95 ~150–250ms on our hosted nodes for the models we demoed. Aditya will run a quick estimate with your token distribution and give expected p95.
- Data retention: Hosted API by default retains logs for 30 days; we can enable shorter retention and strict data isolation options. For customer PII, we offer a setting to disable retention and to route logs to your S3 (Private deployment option recommended for strict controls).

Proposed PoC steps (quick path):
1) I will provision a 2-week Hosted API test key scoped to a single project.
2) Aditya will share a simple curl + node quickstart and a small eval harness you can run locally (we included redwood-quickstart.pdf).
3) We'll set an initial per-key rate limit at 500 req/min for the PoC to avoid throttling; we can tune based on observed patterns.
4) If you want to validate isolation/retention, we can run the same PoC on a Dedicated trial (2-day ramp) or provide Private deployment scoping — but not necessary for initial functional evaluation.

Attachments: SLA-summary.pdf (overview of Dedicated SLAs), redwood-quickstart.pdf, rate-limits.md

Next steps:
- Samantha: confirm you want the Hosted API 2-week key and whether to start with the 500 req/min soft limit.
- Aditya: can you validate p95 estimate and share the quickstart code snippet and SRE checklist?

If helpful I can also set up a 15-min technical sync with Michael (solutions engineering) and Aditya to walk the quickstart.

Thanks,

—Marissa
